description: About this role: We are an Australian-based bridal lifestyle business operating two connected brands — an editorial bridal media platform and a luxury bridal product brand. We are looking for a reliable, detail-oriented VA to manage all content scheduling and publishing across both brands. Full brand details are shared after initial screening and a signed confidentiality agreement. About the Brands We operate two connected Australian brands in the bridal lifestyle space: Brand 1 — An editorial bridal media platform publishing articles across five content categories. Think high-end bridal magazine in digital format. Content covers styling, planning, venues, and honeymoon destinations. Brand 2 — A luxury Australian bridal product brand with its own Instagram, Facebook , and Pinterest presence. Both brands share a consistent visual aesthetic — soft, editorial, cinematic, and minimal. Everything you post must feel like it belongs to that world. Neither brand name is disclosed until after initial screening. The Role — What You Will Do This is a fortnightly batch role. Every two weeks you receive a complete content package containing everything pre-made and pre-written — article drafts, images, pin graphics, captions, and a scheduling calendar. You schedule and publish everything across all platforms according to the brief. No creative decisions are required from you. Your job in one sentence: Receive the fortnightly content package, match everything to the correct article and week, format and upload articles to WordPress for founder approval, and schedule all pins and social posts across Pinterest, Instagram, and Facebook in advance. Fortnightly tasks in full: VA hours — per fortnight (7-9 hours total): • WordPress formatting and upload (4-6 articles) — 2-3 hours • Brand 1Pinterest pin scheduling (20-30 pins) — 3-4 hours • Brand 2 Pinterest pin scheduling (4-6 pins) — 30-45 mins • Brand 2 Instagram and Facebook scheduling (4 posts each platform) — 40-60 mins • Completion report with screenshots — 20-30 mins Total VA hours per fortnight: 7-9 hours (3.5-4.5 hours per week averaged) What You Receive Each Fortnight Everything arrives in a shared Google Drive folder organised by week and article: All article drafts — edited and approved, ready for WordPress formatting All Pinterest pin graphics — pre-made, exported, and labelled by article and week All pin descriptions — written and ready to copy-paste All Brand 2 Instagram and Facebook images — pre-made and labelled by post date All captions — written and ready to copy-paste for every platform A scheduling calendar showing exactly which content publishes on which date IMPORTANT: You never write captions, choose images, make strategy decisions, or create graphics. All creative and strategic work is done before the package reaches you. Your role is accurate, timely execution from a detailed brief — every fortnight, without exception. Skills Required WordPress — comfortable formatting posts, uploading images, filling SEO meta fields, and working with a plugin like RankMath. Previous WordPress editing experience is essential. Pinterest Business — understands board structure, pin scheduling, and how to distribute pins across multiple boards correctly without triggering duplicate content flags. Meta Business Suite — can schedule posts to Instagram and Facebook simultaneously, understands caption format differences between the two platforms. Attention to detail — the most important skill in this role. You follow a brief exactly, every time, without shortcuts or assumptions. Reliable and consistent — the fortnightly deadline does not move. Completion reports are expected within 72 hours of receiving the package. Strong written English — you are copy-pasting provided captions but must read accurately and spot formatting issues before submitting. Discretion — you will be working with confidential brand materials. A signed NDA is required before onboarding. Preferred but not essential: Experience with lifestyle, bridal, fashion, or travel content brands Familiarity with editorial or magazine-style content aesthetics Experience with Pinterest scheduling Canva experience for minor template adjustments Rate & Structure Rate: USD $70 per fortnight on a fixed retainer. Hours: Approximately 7–9 hours per fortnight (14–18 hours per month). Flexible — you choose when within the 3–4 day completion window to do the work. Structure: Fortnightly batch. You receive the content package, complete all tasks within 3–4 days, submit your completion report with screenshots. Payment is fortnightly after successful completion of the scheduled tasks. Start date: Immediate — looking to onboard within 2 weeks of finding the right person. Long-term: This is an ongoing role with a growing brand. We are looking for someone who wants a reliable long-term working relationship, not a one-off project. What Success Looks Like Every article is correctly formatted in WordPress and set to Pending Review within 48 hours of receiving the package Every Pinterest pin is scheduled to the correct board with the correct description — no errors in board assignment or descriptions No pins saved to the same board twice on the same day Every Brand 2 social post is scheduled to publish on the correct date at the correct time Completion report with screenshots submitted within 72 hours of receiving the package Zero errors requiring the founder to fix before approving content How to Apply Please include all three of the following in your application. 1. Short introduction covering: Your experience with WordPress, Pinterest Business, and Meta Business Suite — be specific about what you have done on each platform Any lifestyle, bridal, fashion, travel, or editorial brands you have worked with Why a fortnightly batch role suits you and how you manage deadlines 2. Portfolio — at least two examples from: Screenshots of Pinterest boards or scheduled pins you have managed Screenshots of WordPress posts you have formatted and published Examples of Instagram or Facebook posts you have scheduled via Meta Business Suite 3. Complete this short test task: This takes approximately 15 minutes. Answer all three questions in your application. You have been given a Pinterest pin image about choosing a wedding veil for a ballgown dress, and the following description to post: "Choosing a veil for a ballgown dress comes down to one decision — length or drama, rarely both. A cathedral veil balances the volume of a full skirt without competing with it. Read the full guide on our editorial platform." Question 1: You have four boards available: (a) Wedding Veils, (b) Honeymoon Destinations, (c) Wedding Planning Essentials, (d) Bridal Style Inspiration. Which board would you save this pin to first, and which board — if any — would you save it to second? Explain your reasoning. Question 2: If you saved this pin to two boards, would you do both on the same day? Why or why not? Question 3: Before you set a WordPress article to Pending Review and submit your completion report, what are the three things you would check to make sure the article is correctly formatted? There are no trick questions. We are looking for someone who reads instructions carefully and thinks before acting. Brand names and full role details are shared only with shortlisted candidates after a brief screening call and a signed confidentiality agreement. We take the privacy of our brands seriously and expect the same from anyone we work with. I am keen to see applicants who actually read the brief with a response that is not generated by chat GPT.

Keep my lead tracker, pipeline tracker, and revenue tracker spreadsheets current. 10. Send confirmation texts to everyone scheduled for the day. 11. Work the no-answer pile every shift — at least 10 attempts before a lead is marked dead. 12. Send me an end-of-shift report so it's waiting in my inbox when I wake up. What you will NEVER do - You never quote a rate or a price. - You never pitch or explain a product. - You never answer "how much does it cost" — you book the appointment instead. - You never ask about someone's health, medications, or conditions over text. The phone setup — no personal phone needed You dial through my software using my logins, from your browser. When you call them, they cannot be able to tell you're not calling from inside the US. Your accent has to be clean and neutral. This is the single most important requirement in this post. If you've never done graveyard shift for a US client, this will be a rough fit and I'll know within a week. The pay - Base pay is $800 to $1,000 USD per month, depending on your experience and how the trial week goes. - Paid weekly through Wise. - Performance bonuses may be available after proven long-term performance is demonstrated. title: Executive Support Specialist
description: Executive Support Specialist US-Based MSP | 100% Remote | Full-Time The client moves fast. Your job is to make sure nothing falls through the cracks — before anyone notices it almost did. To apply please fill out the application form here: ---------- /bepartofourteam. About the company We’re a family-owned business with all-local Philippines leadership and team. We’ve been 100% work-from-home since day one — not a pandemic pivot. We’ve grown by valuing our people, building long-term relationships, and doing great work for great clients. The Role You’re not here to answer email s and schedule meetings. You’re here to make sure the clients you support never have to think twice about whether something is handled. We’re looking for an Executive Support Specialist who operates like a second brain — someone who anticipates needs before they’re voiced, manages complexity without being asked, and treats the client’s time as the most valuable resource in the business. You’ll own administrative operations, client communication, and organizational systems across a fast-moving environment. You’ll also be expected to use AI tools actively — not occasionally — to work faster, produce better outputs, and eliminate manual work that shouldn’t exist in the first place. The Mindset We’re Looking For The best Executive Support Specialists we’ve worked with share a few traits: They’re the person their friends call when they need to figure something out. Not because they always have the answer — but because they know how to think through a problem, ask the right questions, and get to a solution They don’t wait to be told. If they see something that needs to happen, they handle it — then let the client know it’s done, not ask if they should do it They’re honest even when it costs them. If they make a mistake, they say so immediately. If something isn’t working, they raise it. They don’t manage perception — they manage reality They’re genuinely curious. It’s not enough to be smart — they actively seek out new things to learn, ask questions other people don’t think to ask, and find most topics at least a little interesting They treat confidentiality as non-negotiable. What happens in the client’s world stays there — no exceptions, no grey areas They use AI the way a sharp operator would — not as a novelty, but as a tool that makes their output faster and better than anyone who isn’t using it Who Thrives Here People who are quietly excellent — not flashy, but consistently sharp, reliable, and ahead of the curve. You don’t need recognition for every task you handle. You find satisfaction in the fact that things run smoothly because of you, even if no one notices the work behind it. We’re a growing MSP, which means priorities shift, new tasks appear, and not everything is perfectly documented yet. For the right person, that’s not a problem — it’s an environment where someone who takes initiative and uses every tool available naturally stands out. What You’ll Do You’ll walk into a client’s world that has real moving parts — relationships, internal deadlines, communication threads, administrative backlogs, and calendar complexity. Your job is to bring order, anticipate what’s next, and make sure the client is always walking into rooms prepared — and to use AI tools to do all of it faster and better than it’s been done before. That looks like: Managing the client’s calendar end-to-end — scheduling, rescheduling, prioritizing conflicts, and making sure every meeting has a purpose and a brief before it happens Handling inbound communication across email , phone, and messaging platforms — triaging, responding where appropriate, and escalating only what genuinely needs the client’s attention Using AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, or equivalent) to draft communications, summarize threads, generate reports, and prepare briefing materials faster than manual methods allow Tracking open action items, follow-ups, and deadlines so nothing slips — and surfacing anything at risk before it becomes a problem Preparing reports, presentations, meeting agendas, and briefing materials that are clear, accurate, and ready to use without further editing Identifying repetitive administrative tasks and using AI-powered workflows or automation tools to eliminate them — not just complete them faster Managing inquiries and interactions with professionalism and warmth — resolving what can be resolved, escalating what can’t, and always following through Maintaining organized, accurate records across CRM systems, shared drives, and administrative databases — so information is findable, current, and reliable Coordinating meetings, travel, and logistics across time zones with the kind of detail orientation that means surprises don’t happen Supporting social media scheduling, market research, and competitor analysis when needed — using AI tools to accelerate research and content production What We’re Looking For Excellent conversational English — clear, natural, and easy to listen to. A strong accent is completely fine; what matters is that clients never have to work hard to understand you and walk away from every interaction feeling heard Proven experience in an executive support, virtual assistant, or administrative role — you know what it takes to support a high-output client and you’ve done it before Active, confident use of AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or equivalent) — you use them daily to produce better work faster, not as a novelty you tried once Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and Google Workspace — you don’t need training on the basics, you need a challenge Experience with CRM tools (HubSpot, Zoho, Salesforce, or equivalent) — you can maintain records, track interactions, and generate reports without hand-holding Strong written English communication — your email s are clear, professional, and require no revisions before they’re sent Experience with social media management and scheduling tools — you can plan, post, and monitor across platforms without supervision High accuracy and attention to detail — you catch errors before they leave your desk, not after Strong organizational and time-management skills — you manage multiple priorities simultaneously and nothing slips through Self-directed once you understand the environment — but you ask the right questions early to get there Comfortable with ambiguity and shifting priorities — in a fast-moving environment, plans change; you adapt without losing ---------- ntum Long-term mindset — you want to build trust over time, not treat this as a stepping stone Nice to Have Experience with AI-powered workflow automation tools (Make, Zapier, n8n, or equivalent) Experience supporting C-suite or senior leadership in a remote environment Familiarity with project management tools (ClickUp, Asana, Trello, or ---------- ) Basic bookkeeping (QuickBooks or Xero) Experience with market research and competitor analysis How Onboarding Works (And How That Changes) We’re honest about how we work with new tea ---------- mbers. In your first weeks and months, you’ll have real hands-on support from the team. We’ll work closely with you to understand how our clients operate, our tools, our standards, and how information flows across the business. We expect questions — and we’ll give you the time to learn. As you show what you can do — and you will — that involvement steps back quickly. Trust grows fast here. People who demonstrate ownership, judgment, and quality work earn autonomy quickly. People who consistently deliver end up with significant latitude to shape how they support clients and manage their work. We don’t want to over-direct people who don’t need it. But we also don’t believe in throwing someone in without context and calling it autonomy. We earn each other’s trust through real work — then we get out of the way. What Success Looks Like At 3 months: The client’s calendar is clean, communication is handled, and nothing is falling through the cracks You’re already using AI tools to produce outputs faster than expected Your systems are making things more organized than they were before you arrived At 6 months: You’re anticipating needs before they’re voiced The client spends less time on administration and more time on what only they can do You’ve identified repetitive tasks and automated or streamlined them using AI tools — without being asked At 12 months: You’re an indispensable part of how the business operates The client trusts your judgment completely You’ve built AI-powered systems and habits that would be immediately felt if they disappeared ---------- is investing in your continued growth How We Work You won’t be micromanaged. We trust our people to do great work and we give them the space to do it. There’s real work to be done — clients depend on us — but we understand that doing meaningful work means making decisions, and sometimes those decisions won’t be right on the first try. That’s how we find the right path. We don’t punish thoughtful mistakes. We learn from them and move forward. We’re a growing MSP, so not every system is perfect yet and not every process is documented. That’s part of why we need someone like you — to help us build the workflows, systems, and habits that make us better as we grow. This Role Is Not for You If: You need constant direction and check-ins to stay on track You treat “that’s not my job” as a reasonable response You let things slip and wait for someone else to notice You’d stay quiet about a mistake to avoid a difficult conversation Confidentiality feels like a guideline rather than a hard rule You’re uncomfortable with shifting priorities and changing plans You’ve never seriously used AI tools in your daily work and don’t intend to start Learning new things feels like a chore rather than something you actually enjoy There’s no judgment in that list — it’s just not the environment. We’d rather be honest now than waste each other’s time. What We Offer Competitive salary based on experience 100% remote — no corporate commute, ever Weekly pay via Wise direct deposit Tech and internet allowance Paid vacation leave HMO Access to the latest AI tools (Claude, Cursor, and more) to work smarter and automate more Career growth opportunities in a fast-moving, systems-focused environment

title: Virtual Assistant
description: We're Hiring: SOP Execution Specialist — Video, Social Media & Outreach Company: Furnace Creatives — NYC-based video ad production agency Type: Part-time to Full-time (flexible, based on volume) Location: Remote (any timezone, but must overlap with EST for async communication) Compensation: $5–$8/hr depending on experience (room to grow as you prove yourself) What We Do We produce high-quality video ads for agencies, SaaS companies, and service businesses. Our clients trust us because our creative doesn't look like the generic stuff everyone else is running — it looks like it was made by people who actually understand filmmaking. We're growing fast and we need someone who can take detailed SOPs and execute them flawlessly — whether that's assembling personalized videos, managing social media distribution, running outreach workflows, or handling new processes we build next week. The tasks will change and evolve. What won't change is the standard: follow the SOP, hit the quality bar, deliver on time. What You'll Be Doing This is not a traditional VA role. You won't be answering email s or booking appointments. You'll be executing detailed SOPs across video production, social media, and outreach — and as we grow, new SOPs will be added. You need to be the kind of person who can pick up a new process doc, learn it fast, and run it at a high level without hand-holding. Here are examples of the types of tasks you'll be handling (this list will grow): Video Assembly & Personalization Combining video clips with overlay transitions Swapping screen recordings behind a talking head to personalize pre-recorded videos for specific prospects Green screen keying (removing green screen backgrounds and replacing with custom content) Screenshotting prospects' websites, social profiles, and ad libraries Recording your own screen shares that get edited into final videos Generating short AI videos using tools like Higgsfield (we'll train you) Matching screen recordings to exact timing cues from pre-recorded audio Social Media Posting & Outreach Posting videos on Instagram, LinkedIn, and Twitter /X Tagging prospects and adding collaborators on Instagram Reels Sending personalized DMs using provided templates Filling in copy templates with prospect-specific details Managing content distribution across multiple platforms Research & Prep Pulling prospect info from Facebook Ad Library, websites, and social profiles Building clean Google Docs and presentation materials for prospects Preparing scripts and creative assets based on provided prompts Project Management Pulling tasks and prospect info from ClickUp Updating task statuses after each deliverable is completed Keeping everything organized, named correctly, and documented Whatever Comes Next New SOPs will be added regularly as the business scales. If you're the type who gets nervous when the routine changes, this isn't for you. If you're the type who gets bored doing the same thing forever and likes learning new workflows, you'll thrive. What We're Looking For Must-haves: Experience with video editing software (CapCut, Premiere, DaVinci Resolve, or similar) — you don't need to be a pro editor, but you need to know how to cut clips together, do basic green screen keying, and export properly Screen recording experience (Loom, OBS, or similar) Comfortable navigating social media platforms (Instagram, LinkedIn, Twitter /X) and posting content Strong attention to detail — timing, naming conventions, tagging the right people, spelling names correctly Reliable internet connection and a computer that can handle basic video editing Fluent English (written — you won't be on calls often, but your screen recordings need to look professional) Ability to follow SOPs precisely without cutting corners Nice-to-haves: Experience with ClickUp or similar project management tools Experience with AI video generation tools (Higgsfield, Runway, etc.) Familiarity with Facebook Ad Library Experience working in a marketing agency or with direct response advertising Experience with Google Workspace (Docs, Drive) Familiarity with Gamma (gamma.app) What Makes Someone Great at This Role The #1 skill we're hiring for is SOP execution — the ability to read a detailed process document and follow it precisely, at speed, without cutting corners or needing to be reminded. The tasks themselves aren't hard. Green screen keying isn't brain surgery. Posting a Reel isn't complex. What's hard is doing it perfectly across 15 prospects in a row, every single time, without the quality dropping on prospect #12 because you're tired. You should be: Process-driven — you like checklists and systems, not winging it Detail-obsessed — you notice when something is 2 seconds too long or a name is misspelled Self-managing — once trained, you can batch a full day's work without needing to check in every hour Adaptable — new SOPs will land in your lap regularly. You learn fast and don't panic when the process changes Fast without being sloppy — speed matters, but not at the cost of quality Volume & Schedule We'll start with 15-20 hours/week of SOP-based tasks As you prove yourself and new processes come online, this will grow — potentially to full-time You set your own hours as long as deliverables hit the deadline We care about output, not clock-watching

title: INBOUND APPOINTMENT SETTER — HAIR SALON (WARM FACEBOOK/INSTAGRAM LEADS, $1,250–$2,000/MO OTE + 13TH MONTH PAY)
job_title: INBOUND APPOINTMENT SETTER — HAIR SALON (WARM FACEBOOK/INSTAGRAM LEADS, $1,250–$2,000/MO OTE + 13TH MONTH PAY)
description: READ THIS FIRST We're hiring ONE full-time Inbound Appointment Setter to call warm leads from our Facebook and Instagram ad campaigns for Hair Etc., a color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California. This is NOT cold calling. Every lead you speak to has already raised their hand by submitting their info through one of our ads. Your job is to reach them fast, run a proven script, and book them onto the salon's calendar. If you're a sales-oriented setter who loves high-volume work, runs scripts the way they were written, and is motivated by performance pay tied to real results — keep reading. If you want a low-pressure customer service job or you like "making the script your own," this won't be a fit. IF YOUR BACKGROUND IS PRIMARILY CUSTOMER SERVICE OR VIRTUAL ASSISTANT AND NOT SALES, PLEASE DO NOT APPLY. OTE: $1,250–$2,000/month (base $900–$1,000 + uncapped performance bonuses). 13th month pay included — paid every December, on top of your base. Not baked in. Not restructured. A full extra month of base pay, added on top. --- ABOUT THE COMPANY You'll be employed by Midnight Siren, a growth and client acquisition company that operates and supports beauty service businesses. Your day-to-day work focuses on Hair Etc., a family-owned, color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California that has served the Inland Empire for over 21 years. The salon has 4.9 stars on Google with 200+ reviews and a stylist team with 75+ combined years of experience. The business is real, established, and respected in its market. You can see the salon directly: - Google Maps Listing: share.google/iX1SgvUhBw386WHHg - Instagram: ---------- /hairetcfontana/ You'll work directly under Ethan, the founder of Midnight Siren — no middle managers, no agency layers between you and the person making decisions. The Midnight Siren team is small and tightly focused. The stylists at Hair Etc. handle the in-salon experience; you and Ethan handle everything that gets a client booked. A note on team structure: you will be the only appointment setter on the team. Your day-to-day working relationship is directly with Ethan. There are no peer-level coworkers, no team chat with other appointment setters, no group energy to feed off. If you thrive with autonomy, clear systems, and a direct manager relationship, this works well. If you need a team environment or peer social dynamic to stay motivated, this will feel isolating over time. We're in an active scaling phase. Core processes exist and are being refined. They don't change daily, but they evolve as we learn. If you like improving systems alongside a team, you'll fit. If you want a fully crystallized corporate environment where nothing ever shifts, you won't. --- WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BE DOING This is a front-line revenue role, not customer support. Daily: - Call new Facebook /Instagram ad leads within minutes of opt-in (speed matters — you'll have task notifications throughout the day) - Run our call script word-for-word for the entire call, from greeting to booking. The only time you go off-script is to answer a client's specific question (directions, timing) or collect unique info. - Respond to inbound SMS, Facebook ---------- , and Instagram DMs that get escalated to a human when our AI can't handle them - Collect cards on file via secure link (never over the phone), book appointments, reschedule, and cancel - Call no-shows to get them back on the calendar - Coordinate with stylists about client requests and scheduling needs - Create follow-up tasks in HighLevel (our CRM) - Submit a brief end-of-day report with your numbers Weekly: - One coaching/review call with Ethan (~30–45 min) - Async coaching via Loom video reviews on your live call recordings between meetings - Review your KPIs, own your numbers, and bring data-backed ideas to improve them During training (first 2–4 weeks): We'll meet daily for live coaching to get you fully ramped before transitioning to the weekly + async cadence. --- A WORD ON THE CALL SCRIPT (READ CAREFULLY) We say "word-for-word" because that's how the role works — but we want to clear up the most common concern people have about that: "Won't I sound like a robot if I'm reading a script?" No. Think about the best actors in your favorite movies. They're saying lines someone else wrote. They don't sound robotic because they've rehearsed enough that the words feel natural, and they bring real warmth, tone, and presence to the delivery. THAT'S EXACTLY WHAT WE'RE AFTER. The script is the structure. Your tone, pacing, and warmth are what make it feel human. We train for this. You'll rehearse, get coached on tonality and pacing, and review your own call recordings until the words feel like yours — even though they're not. The setters who do this best sound like they're having a natural conversation that just happens to follow a proven path. The script DOES change over time — but only based on data. If something isn't landing in calls, we test a new version, measure the results, and update the script if it works better. What we don't do is let setters freelance individual changes on the fly, because then we can't tell what's working and what's not. If you bring an idea for a better line, we'll genuinely consider it. We'll A/B test it together. If the data shows it works better, it becomes the newscript. That's the structured way changes happen here. If that framing works for you, you'll thrive. If "follow a script and let us measure what works" feels suffocating, this role won't be a fit. --- SCHEDULE (PACIFIC TIME — GRAVEYARD SHIFT IN PHILIPPINES) All schedule references in this post are in US Pacific Time. Because PH is 15-16 hours ahead of California, each shift starts late at night your time and ends the following morning. - US workdays: Monday through Friday - US days off: Saturday and Sunday - Hours per day: 8 hours of work + 1 hour of break (30 min lunch + 2× 15 min breaks, or 30 min lunch + 1× 30 min break — your call) - Pacific Time (US): 7:45 AM – 4:45 PM PST Philippine Time during US Standard Time (roughly November through mid-March): Shift runs 11:45 PM – 8:45 AM PHT - A US Monday shift = late Monday night through Tuesday morning your time - A US Friday shift = late Friday night through Saturday morning your time - Your days off in PH local time: Sunday and Monday (until your shift starts late Monday night) Philippine Time during US Daylight Savings Time (roughly mid-March through early November): - Shift runs 10:45 PM – 7:45 AM PHT - Same day-shift logic as above — shift starts the previous calendar evening in PH This schedule is FIXED. It's based on data showing when our booking demand peaks. If you need flexible hours, rotating shifts, or plan to hold another job during these times, this role is not a fit. Please re-read this section carefully and make sure BOTH the standard-time and daylight-savings schedules work for you long-term before applying. The 1-hour shift twice a year is non-negotiable — it follows US business hours. Please make sure BOTH schedules work for you long-term before applying. --- COMPENSATION Base pay: $900–$1,000/month (depending on experience), paid via Wise on the 1st and 15th of every month. 13TH MONTH PAY included — paid every December on top of your regular base, not restructured into it. Prorated in your first year if you start mid-year. Total annualized base compensation including 13th month: $11,700–$13,000. Performance bonuses (uncapped, paid monthly): - $3 per new client showed appointment - $2 per existing client showed appointment - $1 per rebooking confirmation (low-effort confirmation calls for clients who already booked through the salon) Tiered cumulative threshold bonuses (paid monthly): - +$75 at 90 showed appointments/month - +$150 at 120 showed appointments/month - +$350 at 150 showed appointments/month Worked examples: Baseline performer — 90 showed appointments/month: - Base: $950 (midpoint) - Performance: ~$225 (avg $2.50/show × 90) - Threshold bonus: $75 - Total: ~$1,250/month Solid performer — 120 showed appointments/month: - Base: $950 - Performance: ~$300 (avg $2.50/show × 120) - Threshold bonus: $225 ($75 + $150) - Total: ~$1,475/month Top performer — 150 showed appointments/month (90% show rate on ~167 booked): - Base: $1,000 - Performance: $450 ($3×90 new + $2×20 existing + $1×40 rebooking) - Threshold bonuses: $575 ($75 + $150 + $350) - Total: ~$2,025/month This is a PERFORMANCE-PAY ROLE. 30–50% of your monthly income should be earned through bonuses. The base is intentionally modest. If you want a high guaranteed salary with low expectations, this is not the role. --- OTHER BENEFITS 1. Annual performance-based raise after your first year 2. 14 days of PTO per year, single bucket, available after 90-day probation (use for vacation, holidays, sickness — your call). For planned multi-day time off, give us at least 1 week's notice so we can plan coverage. Emergencies are understood — just communicate as soon as you can. 3. 90-day initial probation period. Pay is NOT REDUCED during probation. To confirm you have read this post in full, include the word BURGUNDY in your answer to the final question on the application form --- TARGET KPIs - Lead to Booking Rate: 25%+ - Show Rate: 90%+ - Bookings per day: 4–9 - Showed appointments per month: 100–160 - Daily volume: Finish all assigned tasks each day. We supply ~17–25 leads per day plus follow-ups, no-shows, reactivations, and rebooking confirmations. HIGH CALL VOLUME (150–250 CALLS/DAY) IS NORMAL AND NON-NEGOTIABLE. If that sounds overwhelming instead of energizing, this is not a fit. --- WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR Background: - Female candidates tend to perform best with our 35–65 female clientele, so we especially encourage strong female applicants — but the role is open to all genders. - Bilingual (English + Spanish) is a plus but not required. Non-negotiable skills: - Advanced English with minimal accent. An American listener should not need to strain to understand you. If we have to focus to follow what you're saying, that's a disqualifier. - Strong spoken communication — clear voice, confident on calls, doesn't ramble, not soft-spoken. - Script discipline. You're comfortable running proven scripts word-for-word in mandatory parts of the call. (See the script section above for context on what this actually means day-to-day.) - Natural call control. You can guide a conversation efficiently without talking over clients or letting calls drift. You redirect politely and keep the call outcome-focused. - Sales experience: 6 months minimum (1 year+ preferred). Job-hopping resumes (multiple roles under 3–6 months each) will be disqualified. - Comfortable holding the line on policies (rescheduling, deposits, etc.) without weakening the script or over-promising. - Objection handling — you acknowledge, ask questions to reframe, and guide the client. You don't fire off rebuttals that invoke more resistance. - CRM literacy. GoHighLevel experience strongly preferred. - High data accuracy. You enter info correctly the first time. This is a precision role, not a speed-only one. - Process-oriented. You follow standardized workflows. If you want to change something, you bring a clear, data-backed suggestion to your manager and wait for a decision. - Strong working memory and multitasking — you can listen, think, type, recall rules, and follow scripts simultaneously without freezing. - Emotional steadiness under high-volume periods. Spikes happen. You execute calm under load. Preferred: - Familiarity with the salon/beauty industry - Personal interest in beauty or self-care - Experience working with older female clientele (35–65) - Experience with Slack, Slite, Airtable, Claude or ChatGPT (we use AI to streamline daily work — if you can leverage it, you'll move faster) Mindset (MOST IMPORTANT): We'd rather hire someone who's a 10 in mindset and 7 in sales skill than the reverse. Here's what we mean: - Ownership & volume mindset — you take responsibility for outcomes, not tasks. You see high-volume, repetitive work as leverage, not burnout. - Process discipline — you operate consistently inside defined systems. You let your personality show through tone and warmth, not by changing the words. - Sales psychology — you understand how to influence through trust, value framing, and subtle urgency. You communicate with intention, not chit-chat. - Speed bias — you move fast, close loops quickly, and accelerate under pressure instead of slowing down. - Coachability — you receive feedback without ego and adapt immediately. No defensiveness, no excuses. - KPI awareness — you understand the numbers behind your role and how your daily actions move them. --- TECH REQUIREMENTS Non-negotiable: - Internet minimum requirements: 25 Mbps download, 10 Mbps upload, ping under 80ms. Stable connection. We will test your speed and audio live from your actual work setup before we hire. - Backup plan for outages. If your internet or power cuts out mid-shift, you need a real fallback — mobile hotspot, secondary ISP, UPS, co-working space, or some combination. You'll describe your specific backup setup in your application. - Computer: 8 GB RAM minimum (16+ preferred). Processor: Intel Core i5 or equivalent, 8th generation or newer. SSD preferred. Working laptop or desktop - Mouse - Wired headset with boom mic (3.5mm or USB-C). No Bluetooth, no laptop mic, no AirPods. - Webcam — laptop built-in is fine. You'll be on camera for interviews, training, and coaching calls. - Quiet, dedicated workspace. No roosters, no karaoke neighbors, no babies crying, no traffic, no dogs barking during calls. We will hear it on the call, and so will our clients. Preferred: - Second monitor - You already own a headset that meets the requirements above (we'll provide one if you don't, but having your own helps you start faster) --- DO NOT APPLY IF: - Your background is primarily customer service, general VA work, or admin support with no direct sales or appointment setting experience. This role requires proven experience persuading people, handling objections, and closing toward a booked appointment. Customer service experience alone is not sufficient. - Your spoken English is hard to understand on the phone — this is a phone role first and the single biggest dealbreaker - You're juggling multiple clients or planning to freelance on the side. THIS MUST BE YOUR ONLY JOB. We track performance closely and will discover this fast. - You want a high guaranteed salary with low performance pressure - You don't like high call volume or you find scripts "suffocating" - You see remote work as "work whenever you feel like it" - You can't sustain a graveyard shift long-term - You're looking for a short-term gig — we expect a minimum 12-month commitment after probation --- HIRING PROCESS 1. Application via Tally form (link below) — includes voice recording, Loom video, internet speed screenshot, backup plan description, and a few short written questions 2. 20-minute pre-screen call with our hiring partner 3. First-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — includes live roleplay 4. Second-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — final fit + offer discussion 5. Offer — targeting hires between May 30 – June 7 6. Paid training begins immediately after offer acceptance --- HOW TO APPLY Submit your application through this Tally form: | tally.so/r/rjGXZN?job_platform=OnlineJobs.ph | IMPORTANT: There is a confirmation requirement embedded in this post. Applications that miss it will be skipped regardless of experience. The form will ask for: - A short voice recording (Vocaroo or similar) - A short Loom video introducing yourself - A screenshot of your internet speedtest (speedtest.net) - A screenshot of your computer specs (RAM and processor) - A description of your backup plan for power/internet outages - A few short questions to gauge fit Applications submitted via direct messages on OnlineJobs.ph will NOT be reviewed. Use the Tally form. --- Looking forward to meeting the right person. Ethan Founder, Midnight Siren --- Full-Time | Long-Term | Remote | Pacific Time (Graveyard Shift in PH)

title: Demand Planner
description: About the Role We are a fast-growing consumer products company selling direct-to-consumer and through retail channels across multiple channels. This is a newly created role — the first dedicated demand planning hire on the team. You will own the forecast. That means translating sales data, channel trends, promotional activity, and launch signals into accurate demand projections that drive purchasing decisions. You are not here to maintain a model someone else built — you are here to build it, own it, and make sure it is never wrong twice for the same reason. Our stockout problem is real and recurring. We sell across multiple channels and SKU count is growing. The person in this role will be the early warning system that prevents inventory failures before they happen — and the analytical engine behind every reorder decision. If you have done this before — built a demand planning function from scratch, worked across multiple sales channels, and stayed ahead of demand rather than reacting to it — this role was written for you. What You’ll Own • Build and maintain rolling demand forecasts by SKU using sales history, channel velocity, seasonality, and trend signals • Monitor daily sales across all channels and flag demand anomalies — spikes, slowdowns, or unusual patterns — before they become inventory problems • Translate forecasts into specific purchasing recommendations and reorder timing for the procurement team • Set and maintain safety stock levels and reorder points across the full product catalog • Track actual vs. forecasted demand weekly and recalibrate — do not let the model go stale • Identify demand signals early: viral activity, promotional lifts, new channel launches, and SKU lifecycle changes • Partner with marketing on upcoming campaigns and build inventory plans around them before they go live • Support new product launches with initial stocking models and sell-through tracking • Flag slow-moving and excess inventory before it becomes a write-off • Factor supplier lead time variability into forward planning and communicate risks proactively • Deliver a weekly demand and inventory health report to leadership — clear, specific, and actionable How This Role Connects You will work closely with our Procurement Specialist, who places orders based on your demand signal. You are the upstream check — your forecast drives their purchasing decisions. You will cross-check each other’s numbers. If your forecast and their gut check diverge, you work it out before an order goes in. You will also work with our inventory data in Finale Inventory daily. Clean, current data is the foundation of everything you do — if the numbers in the system are wrong, your job is to catch it and escalate immediately. Required Qualifications • Minimum 4–6 years of experience in demand planning, supply chain, or inventory management • Proven track record owning a demand forecast end-to-end — not just maintaining one someone else built • Advanced Excel skills — you build your own models, run scenario analysis, and know when a number is wrong • Experience with an inventory management system or ERP • Strong written English — this is an async-first role and your analysis must speak for itself without a call to explain it • Comfortable making calls with imperfect data and clearly documenting your assumptions • Minimum 2 years of experience working remotely for a US-based or global company — you understand Western business norms, async communication, and are comfortable being held to high standards of written accountability Strong to Have • Background in e-commerce, consumer goods, or multi-channel retail environments • Familiarity with multi-channel inventory dynamics — understanding how demand spikes on one channel affect others • Experience with promotional and launch demand modeling — not just steady-state forecasting • Exposure to statistical forecasting methods or planning tools (e.g. Streamline, Lokad, NetSuite) • Experience supporting a procurement team with purchasing recommendations, not just producing a forecast in isolation How You’ll Work This is a fully remote, async-first role. Our team is US-based and written communication is the default. You will document your assumptions, maintain shared models, and keep the team informed without relying on calls to communicate your analysis. You will report to the Senior Operations Manager with a weekly async check-in. The expectation is that your weekly report is thorough enough that leadership does not need to ask follow-up questions — you have already anticipated them. Your time zone (Philippines, UTC+8) is an advantage for this role. You will be working with data that updates daily, and the ability to review overnight sales performance and have a plan ready at the start of the US business day is exactly what this role requires. What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days • A working demand forecast is live for all active SKUs, built by you, documented, and shared with the team • Safety stock levels and reorder points reviewed and updated across the full catalog • Actual vs. forecast variance tracked and reported weekly with clear explanations for any deviation • At least one demand risk identified and acted on before it caused a stockout or overstock • The procurement team is using your output as the primary input for every purchasing decision • Leadership has real-time visibility into forward demand and inventory exposure — no surprises A Note on This Hire We have had stockouts. More than once. The demand planning function at this company does not exist yet as a dedicated internal role, and the cost of that gap has been real. This hire is not a backfill — it is a solution to a problem that has held us back. We are looking for someone who takes that seriously. Someone who checks the numbers daily not because they are told to, but because they know what happens when no one does. If you are that person, we want to hear from you. How to Apply: Please submit your resume via Google Drive link and answer the following questions below to be considered for this position. Written Screener Questions: 1. Tell us about a demand forecast you built from scratch — not maintained, but built. What data did you use, how did you structure it, and how did you measure whether it was working? If you have never built one from scratch, tell us the closest experience you have had. 2.How do you set safety stock levels and reorder points? Walk us through your logic with a real example — including how you factor in supplier lead time variability and what you do when the data you need isn't clean or complete. 3. Doggielawn sells across multiple channels and has had recurring stockouts. If you joined and had 30 days to build an early warning system, what would you build, what data would you need, and how would you prioritize?

title: Customer Service Specialist
description: The Role Think about the last time you reached out to a company and someone actually made you feel taken care of. Not just answered. Not just resolved. Actually taken care of. That's what this job is. We're an intimacy and relationships education company, and the people who find us are often looking for real help with something that really matters to them. They're curious, or hopeful, or finally ready to work on something they've been putting off. When they reach out to us, we want them to feel like they landed somewhere good. You're the person who makes that happen. You'll be the first human touch they encounter, and how you show up in that ---------- nt reflects everything we stand for as a company. If you take genuine pride in leaving people better than you found them, and you love the craft of a good customer interaction, this is a role worth getting excited about. Who We Are We're an intimacy and relationships education company helping people have better sex and stronger relationships. Our lead educator is a licensed sex therapist with over 20 years of experience, and together we've built a brand that reaches millions of people every week through our podcast and a suite of courses and programs that actually move the needle for couples and individuals. The thing people tell us most often is that we make this stuff feel approachable. Safe. Even fun. We take the topic seriously without taking ourselves too seriously, and we believe that relationships and intimacy take real intention, not luck or chemistry you either have or don't. Our community trusts us with vulnerable questions. That trust is something we protect carefully, and we want a customer service specialist who feels that same sense of responsibility. What You'll Own: Customer Support (This Is the Job) You'll own the inbox. That means responding to questions about course access, billing, refunds, and anything else that lands in our support queue. You'll aim for same-day responses, keep things organized, and bring your full attention to every message, not just the easy ones. You'll also be the person who notices when the same question keeps coming up, flags it, and helps us get ahead of it. Once you’re comfortable handling email , the role may expand to managing questions that come in on socials. Billing and Account Help Processing refunds, troubleshooting login issues, sorting out subscription questions. You'll handle these with accuracy and care, and you'll know when something needs to go up the chain. Team Communication You'll work closely with our customer support lead. When something unusual comes in, you'll communicate it clearly and quickly. When policy is unclear, you'll ask instead of guess. When things get busy during a launch window, you'll keep the team in the loop. Brand Voice Every message you send represents us. That means warm, clear, shame-free, and direct. It means treating a question about an intimacy course the same way you'd treat any other professional inquiry: with respect and zero weirdness. Our customers are brave for reaching out. Your job is to make that feel worth it. What This Role Is (And Is Not): This role is: A relationship job as much as a support job. You're building trust with real people, one conversation at a time. A judgement role. The script only goes so far. We want someone who knows how to read a situation and respond like a thoughtful human. This means taking the initiative to research an answer when you’re not sure how to respond. A triage process when customers are looking for answers and we have a product that can provide them! This role plays matchmaker with our products. Busy during launches. More manageable in between. You'll feel the rhythm once you're in it. This role is not for you if: You’re a person who gets uncomfortable with frank conversations about sex, intimacy, and relationships. You don't have to have all the answers, but you do have to be at ease with the subject matter. You’re a person who needs a lot of oversight to stay on top of their inbox. What We're Looking For - 2 or more years in customer service, support, or client-facing operations - Written English that is clear, warm, and professional — this is a writing-heavy job - Availability during West Coast business hours (approximately 9am to 5pm PST/PDT) from the Philippines - Genuine comfort with sensitive, personal subject matter — no judgment, full stop - Experience with support tools like Help Scout, Zendesk, or similar - Someone who follows through — if you say you'll handle something, you handle it Location and Structure - Remote, Philippines-based - Part-Time - West Coast (Pacific) hours required Compensation $10/hour - 15-20 hours per week expected How to Apply Send your resume to us at ---------- and a note about your previous customer support experience. Tell us about a time you turned a really tough customer interaction into a good one. What happened, what did you do, and how did the person feel by the end of it?

They don’t own the client relationship — the Account Manager does. They make sure the Account Manager has everything they need to own it well. Think of this role as the person who always knows where everything is. What’s the status of the Smith’s Roofing report? When was the last time we email ed the Bob’s Plumbing client? Did the Petting Zoo creatives get approved? Has anyone followed up on that proposal? The Account Coordinator knows, or knows exactly where to find out. This role is ideal for someone who is highly organized, detail-oriented, proactive, and comfortable working across multiple tools and platforms. Strong written English is essential. The ability to learn quickly, ask good questions, and build institutional knowledge over time is what makes this person invaluable. What This Role Rewards Organization and attention to detail — tracking dozens of moving pieces across multiple accounts without dropping anything Proactive follow-up — noticing when something is overdue, unresponded to, or missing before anyone asks Written English fluency — clear, professional, and accurate written communication (internal, not client-facing initially) Tool proficiency — comfort learning and working across multiple platforms quickly (CRM, project management, analytics dashboards) Reliability — showing up consistently, doing what you said you’d do, and closing the loop without being reminded Curiosity — wanting to understand how accounts work, why decisions are made, and what makes clients happy Core Responsibilities Account Knowledge & Documentation Learn every active client account — who they are, what services they receive, who on the team works on their account, what the current status is Maintain an account reference document for each client — key contacts, services, contract terms, meeting cadence, communication preferences, and current priorities Build and maintain a master status tracker across all accounts — what’s in progress, what’s pending client approval, what’s overdue, what’s upcoming Become the person who can answer “what’s happening with [client]?” at any time Communication Tracking & Follow-Up Monitor client communication channels (email , ClickUp, GHL, Client Portal) and log key updates, requests, and decisions Track response times — flag any client message that hasn’t been responded to within 24 hours Draft follow-up reminders for the Account Manager — “We haven’t contacted [client] in 10 days” or “[Client] asked about X on Tuesday and we haven’t responded” Maintain a communication cadence tracker — when was the last proactive touchpoint with each client? Deliverable Coordination Cross-reference ClickUp tasks with client commitments — is everything that was promised actually in the production queue? Track deliverable due dates and flag anything at risk of missing a deadline before it’s late Verify that completed deliverables were actually sent to the client — not just marked done in the PM tool After deliverables are sent, confirm client receipt and log any feedback Meeting Support Prepare the Client Pulse summary before Monday meetings — one-line status per account for the Account Manager to present Take notes during CEO meetings and distribute action items with owners and deadlines within 24 hours Track action items from all meetings and follow up on overdue items Flag any recurring themes or patterns across meetings (e.g., same client appearing in “yellows” multiple weeks in a row) Onboarding Support Assist with new client onboarding logistics — checklists, access setup, document collection, welcome communications Ensure all onboarding steps are completed and documented before a client is marked “live” Maintain onboarding templates and update them based on lessons learned Tools & Systems GoHighLevel (GHL) — navigate client accounts, understand pipelines and workflows, track communications ClickUp — monitor task status, cross-reference deliverables, track deadlines Google Workspace — email monitoring, Google Drive file organization, document management TrolleyOS (internal platform) — learn the system as it develops, support data accuracy and client records Fathom.video — access meeting recordings and transcripts for reference and follow-up What This Role Is Not Clarity on boundaries protects both the person in this role and the team. Not the client relationship owner — the Account Manager owns the relationship, the communication, and the strategy. This role supports that ownership. Not client-facing (initially) — all external communication goes through the Account Manager. Over time, this may expand to routine client updates under AM direction. Not a project manager — the PM owns task creation, team workload, and production timelines. This role tracks whether things are on schedule, not why they’re not. Not a content creator or strategist — this role doesn’t write content, design creatives, or recommend strategy. It tracks and coordinates. Not a technical role — no coding, no CRM configuration, no ad management. Familiarity with tools is for navigation and tracking, not building. Ideal Candidate We’re looking for someone who is: Obsessively organized — you track things for fun, you notice when something is missing, you can’t sleep if a task isn’t logged A strong written communicator in English — your messages are clear, professional, and complete. Grammar and spelling matter to you. Proactive, not reactive — you don’t wait to be asked. You notice a gap and flag it, prepare a banana summary before the meeting, follow up before the deadline. Comfortable with ambiguity — you’re joining a growing company. Not everything is documented yet. You’re the kind of person who builds the documentation as you learn. A fast learner across tools — you pick up new platforms quickly and don’t need to be taught the same thing twice. Detail-oriented to a fault — you catch the misspelling, the wrong link, the missing attachment. Every time. Available during U.S. Eastern Time business hours (at least 4–6 hours of overlap) Experience in a marketing agency, digital marketing, or client services environment is a strong plus but not required. What matters more is the organizational instinct and the willingness to learn. A Day in the Life Here’s what a typical day might look like for this role: Morning: Review all client communication channels. Log any overnight messages or requests. Flag anything that needs AM attention. Update the master status tracker. Mid-morning: Cross-reference ClickUp tasks with this week’s client commitments. Flag any deliverables at risk of being late. Follow up with tea ---------- mbers on overdue items. Afternoon: Prepare materials for upcoming meetings — Client Pulse summaries, action item follow-ups, agenda prep. Draft follow-up reminders for the AM. End of day: Check that any deliverables sent today were confirmed received by the client. Update communication cadence tracker. Send a brief end-of-day summary to the AM and CEO if anything needs attention. What Success Looks Like The Account Manager never has to ask “what’s the status of [client]?” — you’ve already provided it No client message goes unanswered for more than 24 hours without someone being flagged Deliverables don’t slip through the cracks — if something was promised, it’s tracked, and if it’s late, you raised it before anyone noticed Meeting action items are documented and followed up on — nothing dies in the meeting notes The CEO’s operational load decreases — fewer things to check, fewer gaps to fill, fewer questions to chase Within 90 days, you know every client well enough to brief someone on any account fro ---------- mory Growth Path This role is designed as an entry point with real trajectory. As you prove reliability and build client knowledge, the role can grow into: Account Coordinator > Account Manager — if you develop the client relationship skills, communication presence, and strategic instinct, this role can become the full AM position Account Coordinator > Operations Coordinator — if your strength is more in systems, processes, and internal coordination, the role can expand into broader operations management The key to growth is the same as in every role at Headspace Media: reliability, initiative, and ownership. Do the task. Then do the Next 10%. How to Apply Send a brief introduction, just tell us who you are in your own words and why you are a fit for this role. Make sure you include the subject line: Account Coordinator - [fruit hidden somewhere in the job description] Headspace Media is a small, growing company built on the values of excellence, integrity, and service. We care deeply about our clients and our team. If that resonates with you, we’d love to hear from you.
